about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Mason Jar Chickpea and Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: Layered jar salads that travel well, with the dressing at the bottom to keep everything crisp.

items: 2 x 400g tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, cumin and seasoning in a small bowl.
Divide the dressing among four 500ml jars, then layer in the chickpeas, cucumber, capsicum and tomatoes until each jar is two thirds full.
Add the feta and finish with the spinach, packing it in until the jar is full.
Seal and keep chilled, then shake into a bowl to serve.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Keep jars cold in an insulated bag when travelling.

recipes.title: Train Journey Tuna and Cannellini Lunch Box
recipes.summary: A no-heat tuna and cannellini salad that packs into a container for the journey.

items: 400g tin cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Combine the beans, tuna, celery, tomatoes and parsley in a container.
Add the lemon juice, oil and seasoning and fold gently until the beans are coated.
Seal and keep chilled until ready to eat.
notes: Food safety: keep below 5°C in a cooler bag and eat within 4 hours, or keep refrigerated and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Road Trip Pasta Salad with Pesto and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.summary: A basil pesto pasta salad that holds up well at room temperature.
steps: Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 11 minutes, until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Toss the pasta with the pesto and oil until evenly coated.
Fold through the tomatoes, bocconcini and rocket.
Season and pack into containers.
notes: Food safety: keep chilled in a cooler bag and eat within 2 hours of leaving the fridge.

recipes.title: Picnic Potato Salad with Herbs and Mustard
recipes.summary: A mayo-free potato salad with a mustard vinaigrette, safe for a day outside.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and seasoning in a large bowl.
Toss the warm potatoes through the dressing with the onion until coated.
Cool for 20 minutes, then fold through the herbs.
notes: Without mayonnaise this travels better, but still keep it in a cooler bag and eat within 4 hours.

recipes.title: Airport Friendly Couscous Salad with Dried Apricots
recipes.summary: A dry, light couscous salad with apricots, almonds and mint that packs flat.
steps: Place the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and add the oil, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Fold through the apricots, almonds, mint and cucumber until evenly mixed.
Pack into a container once cool.
notes: Keep a spare lemon wedge in the bag to brighten it up before eating.

recipes.title: Travel Tabbouleh in a Jar
recipes.summary: Parsley-heavy tabbouleh with fine bulgur layered in a jar for easy carrying.
steps: Soak the bulgur in the lemon juice and 100ml water for 15 minutes, until tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Whisk the oil, salt and pepper into the bulgur.
Layer the tomato, spring onion, bulgur, mint and parsley in jars, with the parsley on top.
Seal and chill, then shake to mix before eating.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 day. The bulgur soaks, so prep time includes only chopping.

recipes.title: Camping Corn and Chickpea Salad
recipes.summary: Charred corn and chickpeas with lime and coriander, no refrigeration needed until opened.
steps: Grill the corn over a hot flame or barbecue for 8 minutes, turning until charred in places and tender.
Cut the kernels from the cobs.
Toss the corn with the chickpeas, capsicum, oil, lime juice, paprika and seasoning until coated.
Fold through the avocado and coriander just before serving.
notes: Eat the same day. Add the avocado at the last minute to avoid browning.

recipes.title: Christmas Morning Smoked Salmon Toast Platter
recipes.summary: A festive platter of toasted sourdough, cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers and dill for a relaxed morning.
steps: Toast the sourdough until golden, then cool slightly.
Spread each half with cream cheese.
Arrange the smoked salmon, cucumber, onion, capers and dill on a platter.
Serve with lemon and black pepper so everyone can build their own.
notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon below 5°C until serving, and avoid it during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

recipes.title: Easter Brunch Spinach and Ricotta Tart
recipes.summary: A free-form tart of puff pastry, creamy ricotta, spinach and egg for a holiday table.

items: 150g baby spinach, wilted and squeezed dry

steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line two trays with baking paper.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with the oil for 2 minutes, until soft, then squeeze out all the liquid and chop.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, 2 eggs, cheese, zest, nutmeg and seasoning until smooth.
Place a pastry sheet on each tray, spread with the filling leaving a 2cm border and fold the edges over.
Brush the pastry with the remaining beaten egg and bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and the filling is set.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Mother's Day Baked Eggs in Tomato Cups
recipes.summary: Large tomatoes hollowed and baked with an egg, herbs and a little cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 190C and line a small tray with baking paper.
Slice the tops off the tomatoes, scoop out the centres and season the insides.
Place the tomatoes on the tray and bake for 8 minutes, until just softening.
Spoon a little cream into each, crack in an egg, and top with cheese and pepper.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with chives and serve with sourdough for dipping.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

recipes.title: New Year's Day Ham and Potato Hash
recipes.summary: Crisp potato and leftover ham fried with onion and topped with a fried egg.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes, until just tender, then drain and dry well.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry the potatoes for 10 minutes, turning until golden and crisp.
Add the onion, capsicum, ham and paprika and cook for 6 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the ham is hot.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, then scatter with parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; reheat leftover ham until steaming hot and eat refrigerated ham within 3 days.

recipes.title: Boxing Day Ham and Cheese Breakfast Strata
recipes.summary: A make-ahead bake of bread, leftover ham, cheddar and egg custard.
steps: Butter a 22cm by 30cm baking dish and heat the oven to 180C.
Layer half the bread, ham and cheese in the dish, then repeat with the remainder.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and pepper and pour over, pressing the bread down until it is soaked.
Bake for 45 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes, scatter with chives and cut into squares.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Can be assembled the night before and refrigerated.

recipes.title: Holiday Walnut and Apple Oat Bake
recipes.summary: A tray of baked oats with apple, cinnamon and walnuts that feeds a full house.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 22cm square baking dish.
Mix the oats, apple, walnuts, cinnamon and baking powder in a bowl.
Whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, vanilla and butter, then stir into the oats.
Pour into the dish and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes and cut into squares.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.

recipes.title: Christmas Brunch Potato Galette with Dill Sour Cream and Salmon
recipes.summary: Crisp grated potato rosti topped with sour cream, smoked trout and dill.
steps: Squeeze the grated potato and onion in a clean tea towel until very dry, then mix with the flour and seasoning.
Heat half the oil in a large non-stick frying pan and press in half the mixture, cooking for 8 minutes until deep golden underneath.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes, until crisp and tender in the middle, then repeat with the rest.
Top the wedges with sour cream, salmon, dill and a squeeze of lemon.
notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon refrigerated until serving; avoid in pregnancy or if immunocompromised.

recipes.title: Budget Lentil and Carrot Soup
recipes.summary: A cheap, filling soup of red lentils, carrots and cumin.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until softening, adding the garlic and cumin for the final minute.
Add the lentils and stock and bring to a simmer, skimming until the foam clears.
Simmer for 22 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft.
Blend lightly if you like a thicker texture, then stir through the lemon juice and season.
notes: Costs about a dollar a serve. Freezes for 3 months.

recipes.title: Freezer Batch Minestrone
recipes.summary: A big pot of minestrone to portion and freeze, with pasta added on reheating.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the zucchini and green beans and simmer for 8 minutes, until just tender.
Cool, then portion into freezer containers.
notes: Freeze without pasta. To serve, reheat until steaming and add a handful of cooked small pasta.
Cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Freezer Pumpkin and Red Lentil Soup
recipes.summary: Sweet pumpkin and lentils blended into a velvety soup that freezes beautifully.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, lentils and stock and simmer for 28 minutes, until everything is very soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
Cool before portioning into containers.
notes: Freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming.

recipes.title: Penny-Wise Caraway Cabbage Soup
recipes.summary: Humble cabbage, potato and caraway soup that costs very little.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and caraway for 5 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Add the potato, carrot, cabbage and stock and heat until bubbling.
Simmer for 22 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the vinegar and season to taste.
notes: Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot for a thicker soup.

recipes.title: Freezer Chicken and Vegetable Soup Base
recipes.summary: A shredded chicken and vegetable base to freeze, then add noodles or rice when serving.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 7 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Add the chicken, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot with the peas.
Simmer for 3 minutes, until the peas are tender, then cool and portion.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C in the thickest part; cool and freeze within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes for up to 3 months. Add cooked noodles or rice after reheating.

recipes.title: Budget Bean and Bacon Soup
recipes.summary: A smoky bean soup that uses a little bacon for a lot of flavour.

items: 2 x 400g tins butter beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Fry the bacon in a pot for 5 minutes, until crisp, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and the vegetables are tender.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot and season with pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until it is crisp and cooked through; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.

recipes.title: Freezer Sweet Potato and Coconut Soup
recipes.summary: Sweet potato, coconut milk and a little curry paste, blended and frozen in portions.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then stir in the paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until very soft.
Blend with the coconut milk until smooth.
Season with lime juice and salt, then cool before freezing.
notes: Freezes for 3 months. Reheat gently until steaming.

recipes.title: Budget Egg Drop Soup with Spinach
recipes.summary: Silky egg ribbons in a ginger broth, ready in ten minutes from the pantry.

items: 2 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps: Bring the stock, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a saucepan, until small bubbles break the surface.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Pour in the eggs slowly in a thin stream while stirring until ribbons form and are fully set.
Add the spinach until just wilted, then finish with sesame oil, spring onion and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set throughout the soup.

recipes.title: Hearty Freezer Soup of Beef and Pearl Barley
recipes.summary: A thick beef and barley soup that suits batch cooking and freezing.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches for 6 minutes, until well coloured, then set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Return the beef with the tomato paste, barley, stock and bay leaves.
Simmer gently for 80 minutes, until the beef is tender and the barley is soft.
Season and cool before portioning.
notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and steaming hot throughout; cool and freeze within 2 hours; reheat to 75°C.
Freezes for 3 months. The barley thickens on standing, so add water when reheating.

recipes.title: Pantry Crushed Tomato and Rice Supper Soup
recipes.summary: Tinned tomatoes and a handful of rice make a cheap, comforting supper.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and basil and heat until bubbling.
Stir in the rice and simmer for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Season to taste and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice and soup quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Silky Freezer Leek Soup with Chives
recipes.summary: A silky classic made without cream, perfect for freezing.

items: 3 leeks, white and pale green parts sliced

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the leeks for 10 minutes, until very soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 18 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart when pressed.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and season.
Cool before freezing, and scatter with chives when serving.
notes: Freeze for up to 3 months, and reheat gently until steaming.
